interface.title: phastDNA 1.2.0 (web GUI)
interface.field: Viral genomics / phage–host prediction (bioinformatics, machine learning)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis: training a classifier, then predicting hosts for new virus genomes
interface.what_it_is_for: A form-based front end to phastDNA that builds the command line to train a fastDNA host classifier from host and phage genome folders, with Bayesian search over hyperparameter ranges, or to predict hosts for new virus FASTA files with a trained classifier, and then shows the run as a task page with a progress stepper, run details and console.

data.note: I typed paths to the seeded server-side folders example_data/train_hosts, example_data/train_viruses and example_data/predict_viruses (relative paths, and absolute /work/app/... paths once). The path fields only check that something well formed was typed. They do not check that the path exists, and they accept output folders that do not exist yet. In this environment the backend could not run either mode, so no classifier was produced and no predictions.csv was made or read.

features.name: Bounded-range parameter inputs for optimiser search
features.general: For each tunable setting, enter a lower and an upper bound (equal bounds fix the value). Widened ranges get a marker, and per-field help explains the cost. The ranges go to a Bayesian optimiser. The form does not catch a lower bound above the upper bound.
features.specific: Hyperparameter settings panel: Lower/Upper bound boxes for word vector size, read length, read samples, learning rate, LR update rate, epochs and noise; k-mer min/max sliders; a range icon appears once lower is not equal to upper. The Loss function list is a multi-select; according to the source (phastDNA_gui.py:63-64), choosing more than one loss adds the loss itself to the search space. Learning rate 0.5–0.1 (lower > upper) still showed green.
steps: Open the Hyperparameter settings section
Type a lower and an upper bound for a setting, or leave them equal to fix it
Read the (i) help, which warns that more read samples means longer training
Note the range icon beside settings that will be searched, and check by eye that each lower bound is not above its upper bound
Pick one loss to fix it, or several to have the optimiser search over them
Check the ranges in Parameters preview
serves_tasks: Set the ranges the optimiser may search for each model setting

features.name: Server-path fields with format-only validation and inline help
features.general: Text fields for data and output locations that turn from red to green as you type, with a toggleable help box for each field. The check is on format only: it does not test whether the path exists, and the same green check on the numeric boxes does not catch a lower bound above an upper bound.
features.specific: Path settings: Output, Hosts, Viruses and Classfier path boxes show 'Please fill out this field with a valid path' until filled. The (i) button opens a description such as 'Path to directory with result files'. Made-up paths and a classifier path that was never created both turned green.
steps: Open Path settings
Click (i) to read what the field expects
Type a path relative to the server's working folder, or an absolute one
Watch the field turn from the red 'Please fill out…' message to a green check, which means only that the text is well formed
Confirm separately that the folder or classifier exists on the server
serves_tasks: Point the run at labelled reference data and an output location
Point a prediction run at a model, the query genomes and an output folder, then launch it

features.name: Settings summary drawer before launch
features.general: A slide-out panel that lists every current setting in one place so the run can be checked before it starts
features.specific: Parameters preview opens a 'Current setup' drawer listing paths, threads, every hyperparameter range (for example 'Word vector size 50 - 100'), loss function, iterations and filters
steps: Press Parameters preview

Press Run

screens_never_reached: Train task page: every Train run opened /task as '500 Internal Server Error' (screens/013.webp, screens/026.webp). The reviewer traced this to phastDNA_gui.py:65, where filtered_dict.pop('search_terms') raises KeyError because no form field has that name. According to the source, this page would show an iteration history with the chosen hyperparameters, a top-n accuracy table by taxonomic level, and an accordance score badge, with the best iteration marked.

Predict task page in its finished state (stepper advanced, Elapsed time filled, console log, 'Finished!'). The page stayed at step one with an empty console (screens/021.webp, screens/025.webp). The reviewer found in app.log that phastdna.py crashes on import (Modin cannot import Int64Index from pandas 2.3.3), so the job could not have run even with a real classifier. The classifier path it was given had also never been created.
Any view of the predictions.csv ranked host table. The GUI shows only the file path, not its contents.
not_done: Training a phage-host classifier: every Train launch returned a server 500 (KeyError on the missing 'search_terms' form key at phastDNA_gui.py:65), so no best_classifier was ever made.

Troubleshooting the Train 500 did not help. I tried relative paths on 127.0.0.1; absolute /work/app/example_data/... paths with output /work/app/runs/train2 (no kept screen shows these values); localhost:5000; distinct hyperparameter bounds; Data filter set to None; and all defaults except the paths. Every attempt ended on the 500 page (screens/013.webp, screens/026.webp).

Predicting hosts for Query_PhageA (expected Escherichia coli) or Query_PhageB_ambiguous: the predict run never moved past its first step. The backend crashes on import (Modin vs pandas 2.3.3), and the classifier path runs/train3/best_classifier did not exist.
Choosing the best model from the hyperparameter search (<output>/best_classifier) as the input for prediction: no training run finished.
Comparing predicted host rankings, or the training evaluation by taxonomic level, with ground truth: there was no output, and the GUI has no results viewer for predictions.
Seeing how hyperparameters (k-mer size, read length, embedding dimension) change accuracy: no training run finished.
Flagging ambiguous or low-quality queries: there was no prediction output to inspect.

Not every control got its own try: I left the k-mer min/max sliders, Label filter, Representatives number, Considered hits and the other Data filter options (Hybrid, Debug, General) at their defaults, and did not try the Negative sampling or Hierarchical softmax loss options.
Validation gap seen: a learning-rate lower bound (0.5) above the upper bound (0.1) was still marked valid. I corrected it to 0.05 before launching (screens/023.webp).
